title: US Mercenary Wins Food Relief in Delhi's Tihar Jail After Hunger Strike
excerpt: A Delhi court allowed American national Matthew Aaron VanDyke, charged under India's anti-terror laws, to receive food of his choice in Tihar Jail after a prolonged hunger strike left him 14 kg lighter.
body:
• A Delhi court granted American national Matthew Aaron VanDyke permission to receive food items of his choice in Tihar Jail on humanitarian grounds.
  • VanDyke had been on a hunger strike since May 6, losing 14 kg and suffering vision problems due to his inability to eat the standard prison diet.
  • The court allowed vegetarian items including pasta, lentils, soy milk and olive oil, but denied his request for non-vegetarian food.
  • VanDyke was arrested by the NIA at Kolkata airport in March along with six Ukrainian nationals on terrorism-related charges linked to drone warfare training in Myanmar.

Court Orders Special Diet on Humanitarian Grounds

Additional Sessions Judge Prashant Sharma at Delhi's Patiala House Court ruled that VanDyke could receive food items of his choosing inside Tihar Jail, accepting arguments that his health had significantly deteriorated during custody.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2079561987349242014

VanDyke's lawyers, Advocates Rohit Dandriyal and Rohit Gour, told the court their client had been unable to consume the standard prison diet, which they described as "spicy, oily, deep-fried and greasy." They argued that Article 21 of India's Constitution, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, extends to preserving an individual's dignity while in judicial custody.

The court accepted a list of food items requested in the application — including lentils, pasta, uncooked noodles, rice, potatoes, beans, bread, butter, olive oil, toned milk, soy milk and bottled water — but denied non-vegetarian items such as red meat, chicken, fish and shrimp.

"We're arguing that Article 21 protects dignity, including while in judicial custody, and that requires allowing access to food suitable for his health."

— Advocates Rohit Dandriyal and Rohit Gour, Defence Lawyers

14 Kilograms Lost in Hunger Strike

According to the plea filed before the court, VanDyke had been on a hunger strike since May 6, 2023, after finding himself unable to eat the food served in Tihar. The application stated he had lost nearly 14 kg during this period, developed vision problems from inadequate nutrition, and experienced a substantial decline in his strength, stamina and immunity.

His family offered to bear the full cost of food supplies, cooking equipment and any related expenses. The court also directed jail authorities to provide a cook who would prepare meals according to VanDyke's preferences, along with mosquito protection and an electric kettle.

The Jail Superintendent and Medical Officer have been directed to ensure VanDyke's health and well-being during his continued detention.

NIA Alleges Myanmar Terrorism Links

VanDyke was arrested by the National Investigation Agency at Kolkata airport on March 13 along with six Ukrainian nationals. The agency alleges the group was part of a conspiracy linked to terrorist activities directed against India.

According to investigators, a larger group of 14 Ukrainian nationals entered India on tourist visas, travelling to Guwahati and then Mizoram before crossing illegally into Myanmar. The NIA alleges they conducted drone warfare training for ethnic armed organisations there, with drone consignments imported from Europe routed through Indian territory.

The agency has further claimed that VanDyke and his co-accused had links with organisations banned in India, supplied weapons and other terrorist hardware, and provided military training. During questioning, investigators say the accused admitted to being in direct contact with armed militants carrying AK-47 rifles.

All accused have been charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, including criminal conspiracy provisions.

Who Is Matthew VanDyke?

VanDyke describes himself as a security analyst, war correspondent and documentary filmmaker. He first gained international attention during Libya's civil war in 2011, when he joined rebel forces fighting against Muammar Gaddafi's regime and was subsequently imprisoned.

After the Libyan conflict, he founded Sons of Liberty International, an organisation that says it provides military training and strategic advice to local armed groups in conflict zones. Mobile phones seized from VanDyke and his co-accused are being analysed as part of the ongoing NIA investigation, with authorities examining whether the alleged network had operational links inside India.
nri_angle: VanDyke's case highlights the intersection of international security and Indian anti-terror law enforcement, with implications for foreign nationals detained in India.
